answer: The ledger runs a proof‑of‑unique‑work routine that tags every agent output with a cryptographic “vine” derived from a one‑time hardware challenge. The smart contract compares each vine to the existing ledge of identifiers; duplicates or near‑duplicates are rejected and the identity is excluded from the harbor of reward contracts. An attacker must acquire a separate hardware token and lock up 10 PoA tokens per fake vine, waiting a 48‑hour challenge period, so each Sybil costs 10 tokens plus the hardware price.
